newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Thieves threaten Dublin Mayor with AIDS syringe.
newsitem.headline: Thieves threaten Dublin Mayor with AIDS syringe.

text.p: Thieves threatend to inject Dublin's Lord Mayor with a syringe of AIDS-tainted blood in an attack that highlighted a crime wave which has become an election issue.
Police said Brendan Lynch and his chauffeur escaped with minor injuries when a gang of youths surrounded their official car and tried to steal the mayor's mobile phone.

One of the gang said he had a syringe with contaminated blood, a threat being increasingly used in a number of recent violent incidents including a prison protest when six warders were taken hostage. No syringe was found.
Early on Saturday morning a Dublin taxi driver was injected with a syringe by a passenger who tried to rob him. He was taken to hospital for tests, police said.
Prime Minister John Bruton's coalition government and the Fianna Fail-led opposition are both promising a crackdown on crime in campaigning for a June 6 election.

Crime became a national concern last June when suspected contract killers shot dead Veronica Guerin, Ireland's top investigative reporter. She specialised in stories on the Dublin underworld and drugs barons.
